title: Reconstructing Evidence and Selection from Organica's Surviving State
description: An auditability study of a developmental-structure engine: which of an agent's structural decisions can be reconstructed from its surviving state, and which cannot. The paper measures reconstruction fidelity for three probe arms against three forms of oracle — the engine's own record, a state snapshot, and a structural read — and reports the answer as partially yes: surviving state supports part of the reconstruction, and the rest does not follow. The negative results are the substance: the paper names the limits of the audit trail rather than the reach of the method.
notes: Files: the manuscript as PDF, the manuscript source (Markdown), and the three figures as PDF. The supporting evidence artifacts are in the v0.12.0 software record (v0.9.0 remains the archival reference for the frozen engine) and in the repository.
